assessments.reasoning: The seven contiguous parts of SPDX’s pinned json/details/LGPL-2.1-or-later.json cover 102,067 bytes, SHA-256 77d2ee552d757921500b412707a348d395f4d165b8432d181e080d0a3d7cba9c. Part 1 reports isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 4 gives the exact licenseId, header, and comment that the file’s notice determines the choice. It cites both GNU old-license HTML pages and OSI’s LGPL-2.1 page. The less specific OSI URL does not change the record’s explicit identifier.

The official repository’s annotated v3.29.0 tag targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That SHA matches the later record’s retrieval URL and the claim’s data revision. The tag is unsigned, and its distinct tag-object SHA identifies the annotation.

The two contiguous GNU archive captures report the exact publisher digest in scope. Section 13 explains the recipient’s option when the library specifies a version and “any later version.” The application example explicitly names 2.1 and places the later-version election with the recipient. This supplies publisher context for the SPDX mapping.

challenge.method: Tested a notice naming only version 2.1, a notice omitting the version number, and a copy converted to the ordinary GPL under §3 against the proposed later-version correspondence.
challenge.results: A version-2.1-only notice lacks the later-version election. A versionless notice invokes §13’s separate rule allowing any FSF-published version, which sets no 2.1 floor. Section 3 changes the license family for the affected copy. The proposed identifier fits the specific notice offering 2.1 and later FSF versions.

limitations: The FSF application example illustrates a notice a licensor can adopt. A project’s actual notice must establish its own grant, file coverage, version choice, and modifications. One representation cannot establish the election across all project files.

The generated SPDX text and the GNU archive copy differ in incidental wording, including the FSF postal address versus web references and the sample disclaimer signatory Ty Coon versus Moe Ghoul. The correspondence concerns the edition and election and does not assert byte identity.
reasoning: SPDX License List 3.29.0 records LGPL-2.1-or-later. Its standard header and the FSF application example both offer “either version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.” Section 13 identifies the eligible later versions as those published by the Free Software Foundation. The election belongs to the recipient when the applicable notice offers it. The identifier describes that available choice even if the recipient follows version 2.1.
